Use for ANY edit to a .tex file in a paper or patent\n  repo — reformatting, copy-editing, compressing, polishing, or reviewing\n  someone else's prose edit. Trigger on prompts like \"reformat to use\n  semantic line breaks\", \"copy-editor task: tighten ONLY this file by\n  ~12-15% through prose compression, changing no fact\", \"you are checking a\n  paper edit for prose damage\", \"compress the intro to fit the page\n  budget\", \"polish this paragraph\", \"this sounds not that professional\",\n  or casual asks like \"shorten section 5\" or \"fix the wording here\".\n  Do NOT use for LaTeX build/compile errors, TikZ or figure debugging,\n  BibTeX entry generation or verification (use bib-fetch), read-only\n  claim-level auditing of the paper's content (use paper-scrutiny), or\n  prose outside .tex files (READMEs, Markdown docs, Coq/Lean comments).\n---\n\n# LaTeX editing conventions\n\nApply these rules to every edit of a `.tex` file.\nIf the project's CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md prescribes different conventions, the project docs win — this skill fills the gaps they leave.\nVenue rules (double-blind anonymity, page budget, formatting requirements of e.g. an IEEE S&P submission) likewise override anything below: never add author-identifying text to an anonymized draft, and treat the page budget as a hard constraint.\n\n## Semantic line breaks\n\nPut one sentence per source line; break long sentences at clause boundaries (after commas, semicolons, or before `\\cite`/`\\ref`-heavy tails).\nWhy: version control diffs then show exactly which sentence changed. A reflowed paragraph turns a one-word fix into a 15-line diff that no coauthor can review.\n\n- When editing one sentence, never rewrap the surrounding paragraph.\n- When asked to *reformat* to semantic line breaks, change line breaks only: the text must be word-for-word identical after joining lines. Verify with a whitespace-insensitive diff (e.g. `git diff --word-diff` showing no changes).\n\n## Tighten-by-N% protocol\n\nWhen asked to tighten or compress prose by roughly N%:\n\n1. Edit only the named file or section — scope fences are literal, not suggestions.\n2. Compress by cutting filler (\"it is worth noting that\"), merging redundant sentences, and turning nominalizations into verbs — never by dropping information.\n3. Treat these as invariants that must survive byte-for-byte or meaning-for-meaning:\n   - every number, unit, and tolerance;\n   - all math, inline and display;\n   - every `\\cite`, `\\ref`, `\\eqref`, `\\label` key;\n   - theorem/lemma/definition statements (mathematical content verbatim);\n   - defined terms and notation introduced elsewhere in the paper;\n   - the tense of claims (\"we prove\" vs. \"we will prove\") and the hedging level (\"suggests\" is not \"shows\").\n4. Land within a couple of points of the target. If N% is unreachable without breaking an invariant, stop short and say which invariant blocked you — undershooting is acceptable, changing a fact is not.\n\nWhy the hedging rule gets its own line: compression edits silently upgrade claims (\"our results suggest\" → \"we establish\") more often than they change numbers, and for a paper backed by machine-checked proofs the exact strength of each claim is part of the technical content.\n\n## Wording-only safety check\n\nAfter any copy-edit (yours or one you are reviewing for prose damage), diff old against new and verify zero changes to numbers, math, citation/reference/label keys, theorem statements, and defined terms.\nMake the key check mechanical rather than by eye, e.g.:\n\n```sh\nmkdir -p tmp   # scratch files go in tmp/, never into the paper source tree\ngrep -oE '\\\\[A-Za-z]*(cite|ref|label)[A-Za-z]*\\*?\\{[^}]*\\}' old.tex | sort > tmp/keys.old\ngrep -oE '\\\\[A-Za-z]*(cite|ref|label)[A-Za-z]*\\*?\\{[^}]*\\}' new.tex | sort > tmp/keys.new\ndiff tmp/keys.old tmp/keys.new   # must be empty\n```\n\nThis pattern also catches natbib/cleveref/hyperref variants (`\\citep`, `\\citet`, `\\cref`, `\\Cref`, `\\autoref`, `\\pageref`, starred forms), but optional-argument forms (`\\citep[p.~3]{key}`) escape any brace-anchored pattern — finish with a `git diff --word-diff` scan for cite/ref tokens.\n\nWhy: an edit that improves flow but flips a constant or drops a citation is worse than no edit, and the checklist turns the author's re-review from re-reading into spot-checking.\n\n## Stability and restraint\n\n- Keep `\\label` names and bib keys stable across edits. Other files, coauthors' in-flight branches, and reviewer responses reference them; renaming a label is a repo-wide change, not a copy-edit.\n- Introduce no new macros or packages and do not restructure sections unless explicitly asked. Macro vocabulary and section architecture are paper-level decisions the authors own.\n- Match the paper's existing voice. Reuse its established terminology; when choosing between a punchy adjective and the standard term of art, pick the term of art. Let $\\\\{A^{x,y_1,y_2}_{a_1,\\\\,a_2}\\\\}$ be a family of projective measurements with outcomes $(a_1, a_2) \\\\in \\\\mathcal R_1 \\\\times \\\\mathcal R_2$ such that for $i \\\\in \\\\{1,2\\\\}$,\\n   373\\t\\t\\\\begin{equation}\\\\label{eq:pasting-1}\\n   374\\t\\t\\tA^{x,y_1,y_2}_{a_i} \\\\ot \\\\Id \\\\simeq_\\\\delta \\\\Id \\\\ot (G_i)^x_{[\\\\operatorname{eval}_{y_i}(\\\\cdot)=a_i]}\\n   375\\t\\t\\\\end{equation}\\n   505\\t\\\\label{sec:types}\\n   506\\t\\n   507\\tThe question distribution of the Pauli basis test is \\\\emph{typed}: each question is a pair consisting of a type, drawn together with the other player's type from the edges of a fixed \\\\emph{type graph}, and a question content, drawn from a CL distribution determined by the pair of types.\\n   508\\t\\n   509\\t\\\\begin{definition}[Typed conditionally linear functions]\\\\label{def:typed-cl-functions}\\n   510\\t\\t\\\\uses{def:cl-func}\\n   511\\t\\tLet $\\\\mathcal T$ be a finite set (the \\\\emph{type set}) and let $V$ be $\\\\F^n$ for some integer $n \\\\ge 0$. More generally, for an integer $k$ and tuples $m = (m_1,\\\\ldots,m_k)$, $q = (q_1,\\\\ldots,q_k)$, $d = (d_1,\\\\ldots,d_k)$, let $\\\\mathrm{PolyMeas}(m,q,d,k)$ denote the set of measurements $G = \\\\{G_{g_1,\\\\ldots,g_k}\\\\}$ such that for each $i \\\\in \\\\{1,\\\\ldots,k\\\\}$, the outcome index $g_i$ is a polynomial $g_i\\\\colon \\\\F_{q_i}^{m_i} \\\\to \\\\F_{q_i}$ of individual degree at most $d_i$.\\n   108\\t\\\\end{definition}\\n   109\\t\\n   110\\tQuantum soundness of a version of the classical low-degree test for polynomials of low \\\\emph{total} degree was claimed by Natarajan and Vidick, building on an analysis of a three-prover version of the test by Vidick; there is a known gap in the soundness analysis of that test, and it is not used here. The statement below is the form most directly useful in what follows.\\n   111\\t\\n   112\\t% The paper states this result in a theorem environment with the label lem:ld-soundness.\\n   113\\t% We keep both the environment and the label verbatim for cross-reference fidelity.\\n   114\\t\\\\begin{theorem}[Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low individual degree test]\\\\label{lem:ld-soundness}\\n   115\\t\\t\\\\uses{def:ld-game, def:ld-question-distribution, def:ld-win-predicate, def:ld-meas, def:projective-strategy-general, def:tensor-product-value, def:povm-distance, def:bracket}\\n   116\\t\\tThere exists a function\\n   117\\t\\t\\\\[\\n   118\\t\\t\\t\\\\delta_{\\\\mathrm{ld}}(\\\\eps, q, m, d, k) = a\\\\,(dmk)^a \\\\bigl(\\\\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd}\\\\bigr)\\n   119\\t\\t\\\\]\\n   120\\t\\tfor universal constants $a \\\\ge 1$ and $0 < b \\\\le 1$ such that the following holds. For all $\\\\eps > 0$ and every parameter tuple $\\\\mathsf{ldparams} = (q,m,d,k)$ as in Definition~\\\\ref{def:ld-game} (so $q$ is an admissible field size and $m$ divides $q$), and for all projective strategies $(\\\\psi, A, B)$ that succeed with probability at least $1-\\\\eps$ in the game $\\\\mathcal G^{\\\\mathrm{ld}}_{\\\\mathsf{ldparams}}$, there exist measurements\\n   121\\t\\t\\\\[\\n   122\\t\\t\\tG^w \\\\in \\\\mathrm{PolyMeas}(m,q,d,k)\\n   123\\t\\t\\\\]\\n   124\\t\\ton $\\\\hilb_w$ for $w \\\\in \\\\{\\\\mathrm A,\\\\mathrm B\\\\}$, where by slight abuse of notation $m$, $q$, $d$ denote the constant tuples $(m,\\\\ldots,m)$, $(q,\\\\ldots,q)$, $(d,\\\\ldots,d)$ of length $k$, such that\\n   125\\t\\t\\\\begin{align*}\\n   126\\t\\t\\tA^{\\\\mathsf{Point},\\\\, u}_{a_1,\\\\ldots,a_k} \\\\ot I_{\\\\mathrm B}\\n   127\\t\\t\\t&\\\\approx_{\\\\delta_{\\\\mathrm{ld}}}\\n   128\\t\\t\\tI_{\\\\mathrm A} \\\\ot G^{\\\\mathrm B}_{[(g_1(u),\\\\ldots,g_k(u)) = (a_1,\\\\ldots,a_k)]}\\\\;,\\\\\\\\\\n   129\\t\\t\\tG^{\\\\mathrm A}_{[(g_1(u),\\\\ldots,g_k(u)) = (a_1,\\\\ldots,a_k)]} \\\\ot I_{\\\\mathrm B}\\n   130\\t\\t\\t&\\\\approx_{\\\\delta_{\\\\mathrm{ld}}}\\n   131\\t\\t\\tI_{\\\\mathrm A} \\\\ot B^{\\\\mathsf{Point},\\\\, u}_{a_1,\\\\ldots,a_k}\\\\;,\\\\\\\\\\n   132\\t\\t\\tG^{\\\\mathrm A}_{g_1,\\\\ldots,g_k} \\\\ot I_{\\\\mathrm B}\\n   133\\t\\t\\t&\\\\approx_{\\\\delta_{\\\\mathrm{ld}}}\\n   134\\t\\t\\tI_{\\\\mathrm A} \\\\ot G^{\\\\mathrm B}_{g_1,\\\\ldots,g_k}\\\\;,\\n   135\\t\\t\\\\end{align*}\\n   136\\t\\twhere $\\\\delta_{\\\\mathrm{ld}} = \\\\delta_{\\\\mathrm{ld}}(\\\\eps,q,m,d,k)$, all three approximations are with respect to the state $\\\\ket{\\\\psi}$, and the bracket notation for post-processed outcomes is that of Definition~\\\\ref{def:bracket}. When $\\\\gamma = 0$ the verifier checks commutation directly by asking for both bits simultaneously; when $\\\\gamma = 1$ the verifier checks anticommutation by playing the Magic Square game, using Theorem~\\\\ref{thm:ms-from-ac}.\\n   239\\t\\n   240\\t\\\\begin{definition}[Admissible parameters]\\\\label{def:admissible}\\n   241\\t\\t\\\\uses{def:admissible-size}\\n   242\\t\\tThe tuple $\\\\mathsf{qldparams} = (q,m,d)$ is \\\\emph{admissible} if $q$ is an admissible field size (Definition~\\\\ref{def:admissible-size}) and $m$ divides $q$.\\n   243\\t\\\\end{definition}\\n   244\\t\\n   245\\t\\\\begin{definition}[Question distribution of the Pauli basis test]\\\\label{def:pauli-question-distribution}\\n   246\\t\\t\\\\uses{def:admissible, def:ld-question-distribution, def:ms-game, def:cl-func, def:cl-dist, def:graph-distribution}\\n   247\\t\\t% Admissibility of the full tuple is required here, not only the divisibility m | q:\\n   248\\t\\t% the source parametrizes the Pauli basis test by the tuple qldparams introduced\\n   249\\t\\t% together with Definition def:admissible (references/qpbt-paper/\\n   250\\t\\t% 08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-1075), and both the fixed binary\\n   251\\t\\t% identification of F_q used by the map chi and the trace tr in eq:gamma-value\\n   252\\t\\t% require q to be a power of 2.\\n   253\\t\\tThe game $\\\\mathcal G^{\\\\mathrm{pauli}}$ (also $\\\\mathcal G^{\\\\mathrm{pauli}}_{\\\\mathsf{qldparams}}$) is parametrized by an admissible tuple $\\\\mathsf{qldparams} = (q,m,d)$ (Definition~\\\\ref{def:admissible}): admissibility makes $q$ a power of $2$, so that the field $\\\\F_q$, its fixed identification with binary strings (Chapter~\\\\ref{chap:qpbt-algebra}), and the trace $\\\\tr\\\\colon \\\\F_q \\\\to \\\\F_2$ used by the win predicate below are defined, and it provides the divisibility $m \\\\mid q$ required by the index map $\\\\chi$ of Definition~\\\\ref{def:ld-question-distribution}.   1105	def _github_api_request_paginated(
  1106	    url: str,
  1107	    token: str,
  1108	    *,
  1109	    per_page: int = 100,
  1110	) -> list[dict]:
  1111	    """Make a GET request that follows page-number pagination.
  1112	
  1113	    Returns the concatenated list of all items across pages.  Stops when a
  1114	    page returns fewer than ``per_page`` items (the last page).
  1115	    """
  1116	    items: list[dict] = []
  1117	    page = 1
  1118	    while True:
  1119	        sep = "&" if "?" in url else "?"
  1120	        paged_url = f"{url}{sep}per_page={per_page}&page={page}"
  1121	        resp = _github_api_request("GET", paged_url, token)
  1122	        if resp is None:
  1123	            break
  1124	        if not isinstance(resp, list):
  1125	            # Non-list response (dict, string, …) is unexpected from the
  1126	            # GitHub API for a collection endpoint; treat as end-of-data
  1127	            # rather than wrapping into a one-item list, which would mask
  1128	            # error responses.
  1129	            break
  1130	        if len(resp) == 0:
  1131	            break
  1132	        items.extend(resp)
  1133	        if len(resp) < per_page:
  1134	            break
  1135	        page += 1
  1136	    return items

     2	
     3	Dated bullets, one incident each: symptom → diagnosis → fix → lesson.
     4	This file is the raw feed for `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md`.
     5	
     6	## 2026-08-30
     7	
     8	- **Stale seed clone.** Symptom: files copied from the sibling `../MIPStarRE`
     9	  checkout were dated Jul 5 while upstream main was Aug 25. Diagnosis: the
    10	  local clone's fetched refs were two months old; `git status` against a stale
    11	  `origin/main` looked clean. Fix: `git fetch`, then `git archive origin/main`
    12	  overlay plus replay of upstream deletions. Lesson: verify snapshot freshness
    13	  against the remote SHA (`gh api .../branches/main`) before seeding, not
    14	  against local tracking refs.
    15	- **Warm-cache invalidation by toolchain bump.** The upstream snapshot moved
    16	  to Lean v4.32.0 while the copied `.lake` was built on v4.31.0; the planned
    17	  zero-cost cache seed became a full rebuild (25,052 s, see `builds.jsonl`).
    18	  Lesson: the hot-cache keyhash (lean-toolchain + lake-manifest.json +
    19	  lakefile.toml) is the first thing to check when estimating seed cost.
    20	- **Dirty vendored package blocks `lake exe cache get`.** Symptom: cache
    21	  fetch aborted with "Your local changes ... would be overwritten by
    22	  checkout" for `.lake/packages/proofwidgets/widget/js/lake.trace`.
    23	  Diagnosis: past builds mutate files inside the vendored package's git tree;
    24	  a CoW-copied `.lake` carries that dirt. Fix: `git reset --hard` inside the
    25	  package. Lesson: worktree bootstrap must reset vendored package trees
    26	  before cache fetch (ported into `worktree-setup.sh`).
    27	- **Mathlib cache partial miss.** 20 of ~9k cache files failed to download;
    28	  `lake build` compiled those modules locally. No action needed; noted as a
    29	  normal degraded mode of `lake exe cache get`.
    30	- **Workflow critic stalled on oversized prompt.** Symptom: the study
    31	  workflow's final critic agent made no progress for 6×180 s and the run
    32	  failed after its 7 readers had finished. Diagnosis: the critic prompt
    33	  embedded the full 180 KB merged JSON of all reader results. Fix: harvested
    34	  reader results from the journal; the main session performed the critique
    35	  itself over a rendered digest. Lesson: pass large fan-in data to agents by
    36	  file path, not inline; cap inline context in synthesis prompts.
    37	- **Verification pass caught four live defects in the drafted layer.** The
    38	  7-builder Opus draft passed syntax/smoke on the data layer, but the Fable
    39	  verifier live-demonstrated: (1) the merge gate could never accept a reviewed
    40	  PR (verdict-file glob mismatch); (2) the cap-time forced review was a
    41	  guaranteed no-op (review refused under the fix lock its own caller held);
    42	  (3) three uncoordinated machine-wide build locks; (4) `printf '%04d'` octal
    43	  crash on ids 0008/0009. All fixed same day (`EVOLUTION.md` entry); post-fix
    44	  smoke rerun: issue → PR → green CI fixture → review verdict → merge gate
    45	  PASS → full no-ff merge with bookkeeping. Lesson: multi-agent drafts need an
    46	  adversarial cross-cutting verifier; per-builder self-tests missed every
    47	  cross-script contract break.
    48	- **First warmer run headed for a duplicate 7-hour compile.** Symptom: on its
    49	  first invocation `cache-warmer.sh` cloned the primary repo into
    50	  `hot-main/repo` with an empty `.lake` and would have compiled the whole
    51	  library from source, duplicating the seed build finished the same morning.
    52	  Diagnosis: the drafted warmer had no first-run seeding path — the parent CI
    53	  never needed one because its first cache save came from an ordinary main
    54	  run. Fix: killed the run, added `seed_hot_repo_lake` (copy-on-write clone
    55	  of the primary checkout's `.lake` under a matching keyhash), reran.
    56	  Lesson: every "restore" mechanism needs an answer for the empty-store case;
    57	  cold paths that silently recompute for hours are duplicate-compilation bugs
    58	  even when they terminate correctly.
    59	- **Silent CRLF normalization defeated the split verifier.** Symptom: the
    60	  paper-mirror splitter reported byte-identity, but `cmp` against the arXiv
    61	  source showed every line differing. Diagnosis: the source ships CRLF line
    62	  endings; Python's `read_text` silently normalizes them, so the in-script
    63	  string comparison saw two normalized copies while the emitted files (LF)
    64	  differed from the original (CRLF) by one byte per line. Fix: read bytes,
    65	  normalize CRLF→LF deliberately, verify at byte level modulo exactly that
    66	  normalization, record it in the mirror README. Lesson: verification must
    67	  compare at the representation level of the claim — a byte-level claim needs
    68	  a byte-level check; text-mode I/O is not neutral.
    69	- **Machine slept mid-fleet (stage 3 extraction).** Three readers died with
    70	  "Your computer went to sleep mid-response"; a fourth stalled on retries. The
    71	  two survivors (sec8, sec14a) returned complete inventories. Fix: hold a
    72	  `caffeinate -is` assertion for long agent runs; re-run failed readers via
    73	  workflow resume (cached successes reused) with FILE-based output — large
    74	  inline structured returns remain fragile (second occurrence; the rule from
    75	  the study-fleet incident now also covers agent outputs, not just inputs).
    76	- **First codex review caught three real process defects (PR #0002).** On a
    77	  one-file deletion, the reviewer verified the deletion mathematically (git
    78	  blob identity, alias config, retained note vs paper source) and flagged:
    79	  unfilled Motivation/Description/Testing template in `pr.md`, unfilled bug
    80	  template in the issue, and an `Addresses`/`Closes` divergence between
    81	  the PR record and the commit that would have left the completed issue
    82	  open after merge. All three fixed; verdict machinery
    83	  (CHANGES_REQUESTED → ledger → merge-gate block) worked as specified.
    84	  Lesson: the commit message is not the record — the PR/issue files are
    85	  authoritative for merge bookkeeping, and the reviewer reads them.
    86	- **Registry fork recurred via a stale worktree script copy.** After the
    87	  registry-root fix landed on main, a CI+review chain invoked from inside
    88	  the blueprint worktree ran the branch's pre-fix copies of the scripts and
    89	  forked the registry again. Fix: artifacts relocated; operational rule
    90	  added to `local/README.md` — always invoke workflow tools via the primary
    91	  checkout's path. Lesson: a protocol fix in versioned tooling is not
    92	  deployed until every live branch carries it; invocation discipline (or a
    93	  merge into open branches) bridges the gap.
    94	- **Review-fix loop reached the faithfulness layer (stage 3).** Rounds:
    95	  33 → 26 → 18 findings. Round 1 was mostly writer errors; round 2 mostly
    96	  boundary domains plus register violations introduced by round-1 fixers;
    97	  round 3 exposed two genuine source obstructions (the classical-test
    98	  instantiation at dimension 2m+2 vs the m | q admissibility, and
    99	  supremum attainment in the symmetrization lemma), which per the
   100	  faithfulness policy became the first QPBT paper-gap notes rather than
   101	  silent statement conditioning. The codex reviewer independently enforced
   102	  the parent project's statement-drift discipline.
   103	- **Review loop non-convergent at the tail (PR #0001).** Finding counts by
   104	  round: 33, 26, 18, 12, 17. Rounds 1-2 removed real defects; by round 5 the
   105	  reviewer audited proof sketches of imported theorems at formalization
   106	  depth, invented obligations for heuristic repair sketches in gap notes,
   107	  and relitigated a policy sanctioned in a ledger it cannot see from the
   108	  branch. Diagnosis: a fresh reviewer per round has no memory of prior
   109	  adjudications and unbounded depth on new text; iteration alone does not
   110	  terminate. Fix: review.md gains a round-cap/operator-adjudication rule
   111	  (see EVOLUTION.md) mirroring the parent's bot-fix iteration-cap
   112	  philosophy.
   113	- **`elan show` errors on this machine.** `~/.elan/toolchains/stable` is a
   114	  stale non-symlink directory (Jan 2025); pinned-toolchain resolution is
   115	  unaffected. Left untouched; scripts must not depend on `elan show`.
   116	- **Fable 5 usage limit hit (2026-08-31).** All four 4.2 brief-drafter agents failed at dispatch with the account limit message; the main session continued. Mitigation: subagent fleets fall back to Opus (the standing model policy makes this the default for non-frontier reasoning anyway); codex sessions unaffected. Lesson for the paper: multi-model quotas are a real scheduling constraint — parallelism plans need a per-model budget column.

Diagnosis: `dispatch.sh` truncates untrusted attachments with `head -c`, which cuts at a byte boundary; the QPBT Lean diff is dense with mathematical Unicode, and the cut split a multibyte character — stage-3 TeX diffs were ASCII-heavy, so the latent defect never fired.    120	  installed package, and a system install attempt could not obtain `sudo`;

   123	  `gh auth status` independently reported no authenticated GitHub host; the
   124	  repository deploy key authenticates Git transport, not GitHub API calls.
   125	  Fix: use the explicit user-local binary for preflight and leave API writes
   126	  pending until the owner completes `gh auth login` with the scoped PAT.
   127	  Lesson: migration preflight must check user-local binary discovery, API
   128	  authentication, and SSH Git access separately before attempting installation.
   129	- **The main-session sandbox initially denied the workflow lock root.**
   130	  Symptom: the first `issue_new.py` invocation failed before allocation with

   136	  lifecycle commands and never bypass the locks merely because the repository
   137	  itself is writable.

item.text: The audit is complete; I’m consolidating the findings into the dispatch report now. The central issue is that retryability must be modeled as durable per-operation state, because a single record-level sync flag cannot represent issue creation, PR creation, statuses, reviews, and the post-merge push independently.

    93	### 4. Issue lifecycle
    94	
    95	- `issue_new.py` allocates and completes the local create/classify/scout stages
    96	  first, then ensures the GitHub issue exists with the final title, body, and
    97	  labels.
    98	- Apply only labels that exist in the GitHub repository and report missing
    99	  labels; do not let one absent label abort issue creation.
   100	- Translate local parent identity through the stored mapping. After both
   101	  records exist, use GitHub's sub-issue endpoint to attach the child. A pending
   102	  parent leaves an explicit pending relation for reconciliation.
   103	- `issue_close.py` maps local `not-planned` to GitHub `not_planned` and preserves
   104	  `completed`. It must be safe to retry even when the local issue is already
   105	  closed.
   106	- Remote issue bodies may expose the local id, but generated cross-reference
   107	  footers must use mapped GitHub numbers so `#N` never points to an unrelated
   108	  issue or pull request.
   109	
   110	### 5. Pull-request publication and the empty-branch case
   111	
   112	- Preserve the current operating loop in which the local PR record may be
   113	  opened before the implementation commit exists.
   114	- GitHub rejects a PR whose head has no commits ahead of its base. In that case
   115	  `pr_open.py` creates the local record, marks remote creation pending, and says
   116	  exactly why. It is not an error and must not manufacture a placeholder
   117	  commit.
   118	- Once the branch has a real head, reconciliation publishes the feature branch
   119	  and creates or updates the GitHub PR. `ci.sh` may ensure this publication
   120	  before posting its status.
   121	- Narrow the old push rule explicitly: feature branches may be pushed as PR
   122	  heads; GitHub `main` may advance only after the local merge gate passes.
   123	- Translate `Addresses`/`Closes` footers from local issue ids to mapped GitHub
   124	  issue numbers in the remote PR body.
   125	
   126	### 6. Same-head CI status
   127	
   128	- `ci.sh` publishes a stable context such as `MIPStarRE/local-ci` for the exact
   129	  `HEAD_SHA` in its manifest. Publish `pending` when the run begins and the
   130	  final `success`, `failure`, or `error` after the complete manifest is written.
   131	- Partial/debug runs must not publish a success status.
   132	- Before posting, ensure the commit exists in the remote repository. Never
   133	  attach a result to a different or merely current branch head.
   134	- An ambiguous status POST is reconciled by reading the latest status with the
   135	  same SHA and context before retrying.
   136	- A remote publication failure does not rewrite the local CI conclusion. It
   137	  leaves GitHub synchronization pending and is recoverable from the manifest.
   138	
   139	### 7. Same-head review publication
   140	
   141	- After `review.sh` writes its local verdict files and rechecks the final head,
   142	  publish one review summary tied explicitly to that `HEAD_SHA`.
   143	- The GitHub account that opens these PRs cannot approve its own PR. Therefore
   144	  publish a GitHub `COMMENT` review for every local verdict and state clearly
   145	  that `APPROVED`, `COMMENTED`, or `CHANGES_REQUESTED` is the local gate verdict.
   146	  Do not pretend a GitHub self-approval succeeded.
   147	- Include the exact commit id in the review API request and verify the remote PR
   148	  head first. A mismatch is a refused/pending publication, never a review on a
   149	  stale or different head.
   150	- Include a stable local-PR/head/digest marker. Repeating an identical publish
   151	  is a no-op; a materially different rerun on the same head remains auditable.
   152	- Preserve code/prose lane artifacts locally. The GitHub summary may combine
   153	  them, but it must report the worst local verdict and unresolved finding count.
   154	
   155	### 8. Merge and push ordering
   156	
   157	- `pr_merge.py` continues to run the unchanged local gate and perform the local
   158	  no-fast-forward merge. No remote operation may bypass `run_gate`.
   159	- Replace `github-sync.sh`'s broad `git push --all` with a bounded,
   160	  retry-hardened push of explicit intended refs. Feature-head publication is
   161	  owned by the adapter; the post-merge default is `main`.
   162	- After the local merge, push `main`; GitHub should then recognize the PR as
   163	  merged from commit ancestry. Do not close it through the issue endpoint,
   164	  which would record a closed-unmerged PR.
   165	- If the post-merge push fails, keep the local merge and record remote sync as
   166	  pending. Report that the merge already happened and direct the operator to
   167	  reconciliation; do not invite a second merge attempt.
   168	- Do not delete a remote feature branch until GitHub recognizes the merge. A
   169	  local branch/worktree may be removed under the existing cleanup rules once
   170	  recovery metadata is durable.
   171	
   172	### 9. Protocol and telemetry consistency
   173	
   174	- Update `AGENTS.md`, `local/README.md`, `local/DESIGN.md`,
   175	  `local/personas/main.md`, and the affected protocols so no operative text
   176	  still claims that GitHub operations do not exist.
   177	- Keep `.github/` frozen as workflow precedent; do not reactivate GitHub
   178	  Actions.
   179	- Append an `EVOLUTION.md` implementation entry citing the owner decision and
   180	  issue `#0007`. Amend every enforcement point affected by the changed push,
   181	  authority, kill-switch, and gate semantics.
   182	- Preserve local registry locks, atomic writes, primary-checkout ownership, and
   183	  same-head merge evidence.
   184	
   185	## Required tests
   186	
   187	Add deterministic regression tests under `scripts/tests/`. They must run in a
   188	temporary repository with a fake `gh` selected through configuration and must
   189	never contact or mutate the real GitHub repository.
   190	
   191	Cover at least:
   192	
   193	1. Issue create, marker recovery after an ambiguous create failure, close
   194	   reason translation, existing-label filtering, and sub-issue attachment.
   195	2. PR create/update, the empty-diff deferred case, local-to-GitHub footer
   196	   translation, and recovery of a previously created PR by marker.
   197	3. Missing CLI, unauthenticated CLI, transient retry exhaustion, required-online
   198	   failure, and best-effort pending state.
   199	4. Pending and final same-head commit statuses, identical retry suppression,
   200	   and no success publication for a partial CI run.
   201	5. Review publication with `event=COMMENT`, exact `commit_id`, identical retry
   202	   suppression, worst-verdict combination, and remote-head mismatch refusal.
   203	6. Merge gate still refuses stale CI/review evidence; `github-sync.sh` pushes
   204	   only explicit refs and retries bounded failures.
   205	7. Seed mappings for GitHub issues `#1` through `#4` and PR `#5` are adopted
   206	   without create calls.
   207	8. `local/bin/validate_tree.py` still accepts the extended record schema.
   208	
   209	Prefer focused unit/integration tests of the shared adapter and thin hook tests
   210	for the shell entry points. Do not run a full Lean build for this workflow-only
   211	change unless CI's change gating requires it.
   212	
   213	## Deliverable and report
   214	
   215	Commit the implementation on the issue branch with an imperative conventional
   216	subject. The final orchestrator report must list:
   217	
   218	- files and contracts changed;
   219	- exact fake-`gh` tests run and results;
   220	- local tree/CI checks run and results;
   221	- any operation that remains pending solely because the owner has not completed
   222	  `gh auth login`;
   223	- a concise invariant audit covering local fallback, idempotency, same-head CI,
   224	  same-head review, and merge-before-`main` push.

1	# Local Operations Layer — Architecture
     2	
     3	This repository is a local-only continuation of the workflow that
     4	[LionSR/MIPStarRE](https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE) evolved on GitHub while
     5	formalizing the low individual degree test (LDT, arXiv:2009.12982). The active
     6	track here is the **quantum Pauli basis test (QPBT)** from MIP\*=RE
     7	(arXiv:2001.04383, primary) and NEEXP in MIP\* (arXiv:1904.05870, secondary).
     8	
     9	Every GitHub-hosted operation of the parent workflow is replaced by a local
    10	equivalent. The `.github/` tree is kept **frozen as reference** — it documents
    11	the mechanisms being localized and is never executed here. The operative layer
    12	is this `local/` tree plus the (already-local) `scripts/` audits and
    13	`.githooks/` gates, which port unchanged.
    14	
    15	## Layout
    16	
    17	```
    18	local/
    19	├── DESIGN.md          # this file — architecture and invariants
    20	├── README.md          # operator's entry point: commands, lifecycle walkthrough
    21	├── protocols/         # normative protocol documents
    22	│   ├── meta.md        # how protocols evolve; telemetry duties (read first)
    23	│   ├── build-cache.md # hot main cache; no-duplicate-compilation rules
    24	│   ├── ci.md          # local PR CI gate
    25	│   ├── review.md      # reviewer dispatch and gating
    26	│   ├── autofix.md     # auto-fix loop, iteration caps
    27	│   ├── issues-prs.md  # issue tree and PR registry
    28	│   ├── sessions.md    # agent session naming, dispatch, archiving
    29	│   └── EVOLUTION.md   # dated protocol-amendment ledger (research data)
    30	├── personas/          # system prompts for locally dispatched agents
    31	└── bin/               # executables (the workflow engine)
    32	issues/                # dynamic issue tree (committed)
    33	prs/                   # PR registry (committed)
    34	results/telemetry/     # sessions/stages/builds logs (committed)
    35	```
    36	
    37	Runtime state that must never be committed lives in `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/`
    38	(hot cache, snapshots, locks, served site) and `.worktrees/` (gitignored).
    39	
    40	## GitHub → local mapping
    41	
    42	| GitHub mechanism | Local replacement |
    43	|---|---|
    44	| PR CI (`pr-ci.yml`) on push/PR events | `local/bin/ci.sh <pr-id>` run by the PR lifecycle scripts |
    45	| Main-build actions cache (main-only save, PR restore) | Hot main cache: single-writer warmer + read-only snapshots + APFS copy-on-write clones per worktree (`build-cache.md`) |
    46	| `lake exe cache get` (Mathlib cloud cache) | Unchanged — already local |
    47	| Model-backed PR review chained on CI success | `local/bin/review.sh <pr-id>`: codex CLI with the same `.github/prompts/` review personas, invoked only from a green `ci.sh`; verdict files under `prs/<id>/reviews/` |
    48	| Auto-fix workflows (CI-fix, blueprint-fix, review-fix) | `local/bin/autofix.sh <pr-id> --mode {ci,blueprint,review,auto}` with the same commit-prefix guards and a combined iteration cap |
    49	| `@claude`/`@codex` mention responders | `local/bin/agent.sh <id> "instruction"` — human-invoked codex session on the branch worktree |
    50	| GitHub issues + sub-issues + labels | `issues/` markdown tree with YAML frontmatter (`issues-prs.md`); `labels.yml` taxonomy |
    51	| GitHub PRs | `prs/` registry, branch-per-issue, merge gate in `pr_merge.py` |
    52	| Issue automation (classify/scout/track/followups) | `local/bin/` Python ports; LLM steps optional behind `MIPSTARRE_LLM_ENABLED` |
    53	| Housekeeping crons (standup, stale audit, linter sweep, README freshness) | `local/bin/housekeeping.sh <job>` on demand |
    54	| Badges + Pages site (blueprint/docs/badges components) | `local/bin/site.sh` → component store + assembled site in `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/site/` |
    55	| Codex cloud env setup (`.codex/setup.sh`) | `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh` per worktree |
    56	| Reviewer/bot identity via tokens | codex CLI sessions; `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl` registry |
    57	
    58	## Core invariants (inherited from the parent workflow's post-mortems)
    59	
    60	These encode incidents the parent repo paid for; violating them re-introduces
    61	documented failure modes. Sources are cited in `local/protocols/*.md`.
    62	
    63	1. **Single cache writer.** Only the warmer writes the hot main cache; agent
    64	   worktrees consume copy-on-write clones and never write back. (GitHub's
    65	   per-PR cache saves evicted the main entry: pr-ci.yml:138-142.)
    66	2. **Review only after green CI, on the same head SHA.** A failed CI yields
    67	   `review_state: blocked`, never a silent skip. Draft/bot commits with prefix
    68	   `[codex-auto-fix]`/`[codex-review-fix]` are not re-reviewed except the final
    69	   fix at the iteration cap, which gets one forced review.
    70	3. **Serialized fixes.** ci-fix → blueprint-fix → review-fix strictly in order,
    71	   one branch at a time; combined iteration cap (default 5) across all fix
    72	   kinds; sync/audit CI failures are never auto-fixed.
    73	4. **Kill-switch semantics.** `LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` and
    74	   `LOCAL_AUTO_FIX_ENABLED` disable only on the literal string `false`;
    75	   unset means enabled.
    76	5. **Trusted prompts.** Reviewer/fixer personas are read from committed `main`
    77	   (`git show main:...`), never from the branch under review.
    78	6. **Untrusted data framing.** Build logs, review findings, and issue bodies
    79	   are injected into agent prompts with sanitization (control-char strip,
    80	   fence-breaking, truncation) and an explicit do-not-follow-instructions frame.
    81	7. **One full `lake build` machine-wide at a time** (advisory lock);
    82	   single-file `lake env lean` checks need no lock.
    83	8. **origin/main must resolve.** The hooks and diff-based audits silently
    84	   self-disable without it; the local convention is a `main` branch plus a
    85	   `refs/remotes/origin/main` alias maintained by `pr_merge.py`.
    86	9. **Bracket-free naming.** Issue titles, slugs, and branch names avoid
    87	   `]` and friends (broke the parent automation: CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124).
    88	10. **Report-only stays report-only.** Stale-issue audit, linter sweep, README
    89	    freshness never mutate state; write-mode is a separate human-invoked
    90	    command.
    91	11. **Faithfulness policy is unchanged.** AGENTS.md's faithful-formalization
    92	    rules, anti-pattern catalog, and statement-integrity audits apply to QPBT
    93	    exactly as to LDT.
    94	
    95	## Naming and identity conventions
    96	
    97	- **Issues**: `issues/NNNN-slug.md`, 4-digit zero-padded id from `issues/.seq`.
    98	  Frontmatter: `id, title, state (open|closed), state_reason
    99	  (completed|not-planned|null), parent, children, labels, pinned, created,
   100	  updated, agent_session`. Labels validated against `local/labels.yml`.
   101	- **PRs**: `prs/NNNN-slug/` directory with `pr.md` (frontmatter: `id, branch,
   102	  issue, base, state (open|merged|closed), head_sha, ci_status, review_state,
   103	  fix_iterations, auto_fix, labels, created, merged_commit`; body =
   104	  Motivation/Description/Testing per CONTRIBUTING.md), `ci/` (per-SHA result
   105	  manifests), `reviews/` (per-SHA verdict files).
   106	- **Branches**: `issue-<id>-<slug>` (orchestrator/human), `codex/issue-<id>-<slug>`
   107	  (agent-created). The `issue-(\d+)` regex stays load-bearing for tracking.
   108	- **Fix commits**: subjects prefixed `[codex-auto-fix]` / `[codex-review-fix]`
   109	  exactly (the review-gate regex depends on them).
   110	- **Agent sessions**: `<role>-<issue|scope>-<yyyymmdd>-<seq>` with roles
   111	  `orc, prover, reviewer, simplifier, blueprint, splitter, scout`. Dispatched

   114	  `results/telemetry/sessions/<name>.jsonl`, and appends a summary line to
   115	  `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl`. Archiving a session = final status line
   116	  in the registry + worktree removal; the JSONL capture is the archive.
   117	
   118	## Telemetry (research-paper data)

   122	- `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl` — one line per agent session: name, role,
   123	  issue/pr, thread_id, start/end, wall seconds, token usage (input, cached,

1	# Protocol — local PR CI
     2	
     3	Normative protocol for `local/bin/ci.sh`, the local replacement for
     4	`.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml` (frozen under `.github/`, never executed here).
     5	Read `meta.md` first; `build-cache.md` owns the hot-main cache this protocol
     6	consumes but never writes.
     7	
     8	`ci.sh <pr-id>` is the **only** thing allowed to set `ci_status` in a PR
     9	record. Everything downstream — `review.sh` (invariant 2: review only after
    10	green CI on the same head SHA), `autofix.sh` (invariant 3: sync/audit failures
    11	are never auto-fixed), and the merge gate in `pr_merge.py` — reads the manifest
    12	this script writes and nothing else.
    13	
    14	## 1. What it is
    15	
    16	The parent repository consolidated seven workflows into one so that a pull
    17	request produces exactly **one** CI completion event, which the auto-fix
    18	dispatcher keys off (`pr-ci.yml:3-8`). The local port keeps that property: one
    19	invocation, one manifest, one exit code.
    20	
    21	```
    22	local/bin/ci.sh <pr-id> [--worktree PATH] [--base REF] [--only STEP]
    23	                        [--force-all] [--skip-build] [--dry-run]
    24	```
    25	
    26	`<pr-id>` is `7`, `0007`, or `0007-slug`; the script resolves it to a single
    27	directory under `prs/`, reads `branch` and `base` from `pr.md` frontmatter,
    28	finds the branch's worktree (via `git worktree list`, falling back to
    29	`.worktrees/<branch with / → ->`), and runs everything **inside that
    30	worktree**. Nothing is run in the primary checkout.
    31	
    32	Exit status: `0` all gating steps passed or were legitimately skipped; `1` at
    33	least one gating step failed or could not run; `2` the run could not start
    34	(unknown PR id, missing worktree, unresolvable base).

   136	The guard has one deliberate hole.  `pr-review.yml:69-72` says: *we only want
   137	to review human-authored pushes and the final bot-fix result (detected by
   138	iteration cap)*.  Without that exception, the last fix commit — the one that
   139	ships — is the only commit on the branch nobody ever reviewed.  So `autofix.sh`

   143	that holder would otherwise be the very process asking for the review.
   144	`--force-review` is the only way past rung 9.  Do not use it to "just get a
   145	review" of a bot commit; that reopens the cascade one commit at a time.

## Audit Result

Issue #0007 has a coherent target design, but the current scripts are not ready for GitHub write-through operation. A shared adapter plus durable per-operation reconciliation state is required; adding isolated `gh` calls would leave ambiguous creates, post-merge push failures, and concurrent same-head publications unrecoverable.

### Cross-Script Contracts

| Owner | Required contract |
|---|---|
| [track.py](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/local/bin/track.py:520) | Own flat GitHub identity fields, atomic updates, validation, locks, and the durable synchronization journal. |
| [issue_new.py](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/local/bin/issue_new.py) | Finish local creation, classification, scouting, and parent updates first; then ensure the marked GitHub issue, filter unavailable labels, and enqueue the parent relation. |
| [issue_close.py](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/local/bin/issue_close.py:60) | Persist local closure first; reconcile GitHub even when already locally closed; map `not-planned` to `not_planned`. |
| [pr_open.py](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/local/bin/pr_open.py) | Create exactly one local PR per branch. Publish only after the branch is ahead of base and issue mappings exist; otherwise retain a pending operation. |
| [ci.sh](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/local/bin/ci.sh:733) | A complete exact-SHA manifest is the publication source. Ensure the commit remotely, then publish canonical pending/final statuses. Partial runs never publish to the canonical context. |
| [review.sh](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/local/bin/review.sh:414) | Consume exact-SHA successful CI, write local lane verdicts, combine the worst result, then publish a `COMMENT` review for that exact remote head. |
| [pr_merge.py](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/local/bin/pr_merge.py:201) | Parse exact-SHA gate evidence, merge locally with `--no-ff`, durably record the merge and pending push, push only `main`, then verify GitHub recognizes the PR as merged. |
| Reconciler | Retry one issue, one PR, or all pending operations. It must never allocate another local record, rerun a merge, or silently retarget an operation to a newer SHA. |
| [github-sync.sh](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/local/bin/github-sync.sh:11) | Become an explicit-ref push wrapper used by the adapter. It must not add arbitrary refs or use `git push --all`. |

### Data Model

Use flat optional frontmatter fields because the shell helpers operate on top-level scalars:

```yaml
github_repo: Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A
github_number: 7
github_database_id: 123456789
github_url: https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/issues/7
github_sync: pending        # pending | synced | conflict
github_sync_reason: null
github_sync_updated_at: 2026-08-31T...
```

Local issue and PR numbers must never imply GitHub numbers: GitHub issues and PRs share one number namespace, while the local sequences are separate. Seed these fields from [github-migration-map.md](/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/results/telemetry/github-migration-map.md), rather than parsing that prose file during normal operation.

A record-level `github_sync` flag is only an aggregate. Add a durable, registry-owned operation journal, preferably one atomic sidecar per entity. Each operation needs a deterministic key, payload digest, prerequisites, state (`pending`, `applying`, `synced`, `superseded`, `conflict`), attempt count, remote object ID, timestamps, and classified last error. Keys should distinguish `issue.ensure`, `issue.parent`, `pr.head`, `pr.ensure`, `ci:<sha>:<context>`, `review:<sha>:<digest>`, and `merge.main:<merge-sha>`.

Define field ownership explicitly. Local records own workflow state, gate evidence, generated bodies, and desired labels; GitHub owns assigned identities and observed remote state. The brief does not define inbound synchronization for human edits made directly on GitHub. If those edits must update the offline registry, a separate explicit import policy is still needed.

### Idempotent Retry

Every command should commit the local mutation and pending operation before network access. Best-effort mode exits successfully with an actionable pending warning; required-online mode exits nonzero without rolling back local state.

Before creates, and after any ambiguous result, paginate the authoritative REST listing and match the stable local marker. Adopt one match, create on zero matches, and stop with `conflict` on multiple matches. Updates use GET, compare, PATCH, and verification. GitHub sub-issue attachment requires the child’s numeric database ID, not its issue number ([GitHub sub-issues API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/sub-issues)).

Classify failures: retry timeouts, connection failures, `429`, and `5xx` with bounded exponential backoff; retain missing CLI, unauthenticated CLI, validation failures, and other permanent `4xx` responses as loud pending/conflict states. After an ambiguous status or review POST, query the exact SHA/context or marker/digest before retrying.

Commit statuses are append-only and interpreted by SHA plus context, so identical latest states should be suppressed ([GitHub commit-status API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/commits/statuses?apiVersion=2022-11-28)).

### Empty-Branch PRs

The current `pr_open.py` can create a local record with an unresolved or null head. Preserve that behavior, but detect `base..head` having zero commits and record `pr.ensure` as pending with reason `waiting_for_head`. Do not push and do not manufacture a placeholder commit.

After the first real commit, reconciliation pushes only the feature ref, translates local issue footers through stored mappings, and creates or adopts the marked GitHub PR. Re-running `pr_open.py` currently allocates another local PR, so active branch uniqueness or an explicit “reuse existing record” check is also required.

### Same-Head Publication

- CI: publish `MIPStarRE/local-ci` only for the manifest’s SHA after verifying the complete manifest, `partial: false`, matching local record and branch tip, and remote commit existence. A mapped PR head mismatch leaves publication pending; it must never cause publication on the newer SHA.
- Review: require successful exact-SHA CI, exact-SHA lane files, a final local branch check, and `remote head == commit_id`. Always use `event=COMMENT`; the body reports the local verdict and unresolved count. GitHub authors cannot approve their own PRs ([GitHub review documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/reviewing-changes-in-pull-requests/about-pull-request-reviews?apiVersion=2022-11-28)).
- Identical marker/digest publications are no-ops. A materially changed review on the same SHA receives a new auditable COMMENT review.
- Current race gaps: `ci.sh` does not recheck the branch tip before final success, and `review.sh` finally rechecks only `pr.md`’s `head_sha`, not the actual branch tip.

### Merge and Push Ordering

1. Parse and validate the exact manifest and review files inside `run_gate`.
2. Persist a merge intent containing base tip and reviewed head.
3. Perform the local `git merge --no-ff`.
4. Atomically record `state: merged`, `merged_commit`, and a pending main-push operation.
5. Push only `refs/heads/main:refs/heads/main` with ordinary fast-forward protection.
6. Resolve ambiguous pushes by querying remote `main`; retry only when it remains safely behind, and mark divergence as conflict.
7. Verify GitHub reports the PR merged through commit ancestry. Do not close it through the issue endpoint. GitHub documents that a locally merged branch pushed to the default branch can mark the PR merged ([GitHub merge documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/incorporating-changes-from-a-pull-request/about-pull-request-merges?source=post_page---------------------------)).
8. Only then synchronize issue closures and permit remote feature-branch deletion. Local cleanup may proceed once recovery metadata is durable.
